subject: Trial pathway sync & dry-run plan for CloudHealth AI - deployment mode decision
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.inference>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@cloudhealth.ai>, Priya Singh <priya.s@cloudhealth.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.inference>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Next steps: Trial pathway sync & dry-run plan for CloudHealth AI - deployment mode decision
Attachments: trial-checklist.xlsx (spreadsheet), network-requirements.pdf (pdf)

Hi Alex and Priya —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and a proposed path forward so we all have a single view: the core decision you flagged is deployment mode (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private VPC/on-prem). Based on the needs you described (PII-sensitive telemetry, 99.9% SLA requirement for inference endpoints, and steady throughput during business hours), I recommend a two-stage trial: a short hosted "dry run" to validate integration and traffic patterns followed by a 3-week Dedicated capacity trial with a Private VPC gating step if security clears it.

Key success criteria (proposed) — please confirm or edit:
- Functional: end-to-end integration with your API gateway and auth flow; all endpoints return correct inference for our canned prompts (pass/fail).
- Performance: median P95 latency < 200ms for 1k concurrent requests across our sample load profile.
- Cost signal: projected $/1M tokens using continuous-batch configuration vs baseline.
- Security/compliance: KV cache/data-at-rest validations and audit log capture in Private VPC mode; SOC2 evidence where needed.

Stakeholders and owners:
- CloudHealth: Alex Turner (product lead), Priya Singh (security/compliance), procurement@cloudhealth.ai (contracts)
- Redwood: Irene Choi (AE, owner), Ben Carter (SE, technical lead), Soojin Lee (solutions/ops)

Timing (proposed):
- Week 0 (kickoff): finalize trial checklist, share sanitized sample payloads, get network egress rules in place (2 business days)
- Week 1: Hosted dry run (validate auth, latency sampling, baseline)
- Week 2-4: Dedicated trial (configured capacity); if security sign-off provided in Week 1, we will run the Dedicated trial inside Private VPC in Week 2-4; otherwise Dedicated in Redwood-managed VPC and parallel security review for Private.

Immediate next steps I suggest we confirm this week:
1) Alex/Priya: confirm whether security requires Private VPC from day 1 or if a hosted dry run is acceptable.
2) Procurement: confirm NDA/MoU timeline (cc'd procurement alias if helpful).
3) Ben: I will ask you to prepare the smoke-test checklist and a short runbook for the dry run.

I've attached a concise trial-checklist.xlsx and network-requirements.pdf to help accelerate the kickoff. If this looks good, can we lock a 30-min kickoff on Monday, July 12 to align engineers and security?

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,
Irene Choi
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.inference
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0197

---
Note: if security requires on-prem/private from day 1, we can instead propose a 2-week Private VPC-only proof with an extended lead time for network approvals (estimated 10 business days).

From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@cloudhealth.ai>

Subject: Re: Next steps: Trial pathway sync & dry-run plan for CloudHealth AI - deployment mode decision
Attachments: security-questionnaire-short.xlsx (we've attached our security team's short form)

Thanks, Irene — good recap. A few clarifications from our side after discussing with Priya:

1) Security posture: our security team is leaning heavily toward Private VPC for any workloads that touch identifiable telemetry. They asked whether Private VPC can be available for the Dedicated trial (not just later). If so, what is the realistic lead time for Private VPC setup?

2) Procurement: same thread — we will need an estimate for committed-month pricing vs burst (Dedicated) and a short MoU to start review. procurement@cloudhealth.ai will circulate items if you can produce the MoU template.

3) Hosted dry run: Priya asked if we can run the hosted dry run in a dev namespace where no telemetry leaves the account (we would stub data). If Private VPC is a hard requirement, we need to know if the hosted step is optional or still recommended.

We attached our abbreviated security questionnaire. Priya will take point on that with your Soojin/Ben.

Alex
Alex Turner
Director, Product | CloudHealth AI
alex.turner@cloudhealth.ai

Subject: RE: Next steps: Trial pathway sync & dry-run plan for CloudHealth AI - deployment mode decision
Attachments: poc-smoke-tests.md (text), network-requirements.pdf (redwood annotated)

Hi Alex/Priya —

Thanks for the quick response and for the security questionnaire — Soojin and I will review this with your team. A few technical notes so expectations are aligned:

Private VPC lead time:~ 8-10 business days for provisioning + network rule testing once we receive the allowlist and peering details. If you need Private inside your cloud account (customer-hosted VPC), that adds an integration step we estimate an additional 4-6 business days.

Hosted dry-run: fully feasible in a dev/sandbox namespace with stubbed payloads to validate auth & integration. It will not exercise data residency/audit log validations required by security, but it's extremely useful to validate performance and integration early.

Dedicated trial config (recommended if you want predictable throughput):
- GPU pool sized for 100 r/s sustained peak with headroom for 200 r/s burst (we'll tune after baseline)
- Continuous batching enabled + KV cache configured for repeated prompt prefixes
- Metrics collection: per-route latency, per-token cost estimate and trace logs (we'll provide a lightweight tracing hook)

Smoke test checklist highlights (attached poc-smoke-tests.md):
- Auth token rotation and expiry handling
- Sample inference end-to-end (10 prompts, pass criteria: correct labels)
- Load sample (ramp to 100 r/s over 10 mins) and measure P95
- Failover: simulate a single-node failure and verify automatic fallback to compatible model variant

If Private VPC is required from the start, recommended path: submit allowlist and peering info today -> Redwood provisions Private endpoint -> security runs quick validation -> we start Dedicated trial inside Private VPC.

I'll be available for a technical kickoff on Mon, Jul 12 — suggest a 45-min slot to include your infra/security engineers.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.inference

Thanks all — quick alignment from security/procurement:

1) Security stance: Private VPC is preferred for any PII-touching flow. We are OK with a hosted dry run in a sandbox if (a) no real telemetry is used and (b) the aim is only integration/perf validation. Private VPC for the Dedicated trial is preferred but we can sign off on a staged approach (hosted dry run -> Dedicated (Redwood VPC) -> Private VPC Dedicated) if the lead time for Private provisioning is an issue.

2) Timeline: we can target the dry-run dev week July 12-16. If Private VPC provisioning completes by July 23, we can run Dedicated Private VPC July 26-Aug 13. Procurement will review MoU and get back by EOD Fri with redlines.

3) Action items:
- CloudHealth (Priya): share the sanitized sample payloads and the allowlist/peering info for Private provisioning by EOD Tue, Jul 13.
- Redwood (Irene/Ben/Soojin): provide the MoU draft and a cost estimate for Dedicated capacity (committed vs burst) by Fri, Jul 9.
- Schedule: please propose a 45-min kickoff on Mon Jul 12 (Irene, can you send times?)

We'll loop infra and security into the kickoff invite once times are confirmed.

Priya Singh
Head of Security & Compliance | CloudHealth AI
priya.s@cloudhealth.ai
